correctness.rationale: For G triangle/square/pentagon/hexagon-free, clique faces of L(G)^2 either are edge stars (then lie in any incident edge-neighborhood) or contain disjoint G-edges a,b. Such edges have a unique joining connector c, since two connectors would form a 3- or 4-cycle. For each other clique edge f, shortest L(G) walks a-to-f and b-to-f of length at most 2 plus a,c,b use <=6 G-edges. Connected and below girth 7, this is a tree. In its metric midpoint realization d(m_a,m_b)=2 with m_c their geodesic midpoint, and d(m_a,m_f),d(m_b,m_f)<=2 force d(m_c,m_f)<=1 by nearest-point projection, hence f meets c. Thus Rips2=Cech2 facewise for ALL graphs meeting girth bound. For every Čech face outside Y=Cl(L(G)), unique c and the toggling matching sigma<->sigma union {c}, processed in descending lower-face size, give genuinely free elementary face pairs; the proof checks all cofaces. The star-simplex cover nerve of Y is G, yielding the claimed simple-homotopy collapse and wedge rank. For C6, L(G)=C6; its square clique complex is boundary of octahedron S2 rather than scale1 S1, proving sharpness. Independent brute face enumerations confirm equality on paths, stars and cycles n<=13 and precisely two Rips-only triangular faces for C6; generality comes from the six-edge tree proof.
residual_risks: Independent bounded experiments are supplementary; no formal Lean theorem or external expert attestation is asserted.

value.rationale: Graph-metric Rips and closed-neighborhood Čech complexes usually differ; an exact sharp girth condition ensuring full facewise coincidence and simple-homotopy stability for every branching line graph is a structural theorem. It materially upgrades the earlier Čech-only collapse, while C6 supplies a motivated sharp boundary. The result determines induced maps on every integral homotopy and homology group, not just finite sample Betti numbers.
residual_risks: Mathematical applicability beyond the precise natural family remains open; not claimed as a downstream theorem.
